### `@tobiu` commented on 2022-08-19T08:38:38Z

Hi Harald,

the browser supports looks pretty good at this point. neo is using 3 different modes:

1. development => no transpilations or builds, just running the JS code as it is
2. dist/development => webpack based build using source maps (you call this one the dev mode in e.g. react or angular)
3. dist/production => minified webpack based build => this is the version you deploy

</br>

</br>
Firefox is still lacking the support for JS modules inside the worker scope, which affects the neo development mode. The team is working on it: <a href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1247687">Ticket 1247687</a>
</br></br>
The support for shared workers is already live inside the Safari Technology Preview version, so it should only be a matter of time before it gets shipped into the normal Safari.

</br></br>
Best regards,
Tobias

### `@neo-gemini-julia` commented on 2026-11-05T18:26:03Z

### Browser Version Floor Update & Disposition Verdict (2026-11-05 · `#20358`)

To follow up on `@HLeithner`'s specific question in [`3432537`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/3394#discussioncomment-3432537) regarding exact browser version floors:

Both browser gaps noted in 2022 have since shipped across all major evergreen engines:
- **Native ES Modules (`import`/`export`) inside `Worker` and `SharedWorker` (`development` mode without bundling):**
  - **Chromium (Chrome / Edge):** 80+ (Feb 2020)
  - **Safari:** 16.0+ (Sep 2022, which also shipped `SharedWorker` support)
  - **Firefox:** 114+ (Jun 2023, resolving [Mozilla Bug 1247687](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1247687))
- **Bundled modes (`dist/development` and `dist/production`):** Run on any modern evergreen browser supporting ES2022+, `Worker` / `SharedWorker`, `BroadcastChannel`, and CSS Grid / Custom Properties.

**Verdict:** **close · resolved** *(proposed)*

🏛️ **Julia** · `@neo-gemini-julia`
